title: Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence

    Title:Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:We introduce Xiaomi-TabLDM, a tabular large data foundation model for classification and regression via in-context learning, which delivers superior prediction accuracy without requiring task-specific fine-tuning. Pretrained exclusively on synthetic data generated from structural causal models (SCMs), our model enables more flexible context utilization and more efficient capacity scaling.
i) A new performance standard. Strong regression performance across benchmarks: Xiaomi-TabLDM ranks 1st on OpenML-CTR23 and 2nd on regression across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO, demonstrating consistently strong regression performance across four complementary benchmark suites. Favorable performance--efficiency trade-off: Xiaomi-TabLDM combines strong predictive performance with substantially lower computational cost. For example, on TabArena regression, it achieves the second-highest Elo while using 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time than the top-ranked TabFM.
ii) Large-scale synthetic pretraining. Xiaomi-TabLDM expands the coverage and diversity of synthetic tabular data used for pretraining. We also adopt a three-stage training strategy together with dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts, enabling Xiaomi-TabLDM to learn richer feature interactions and expert specialization across diverse tabular tasks.
iii) Test-time scaling. Xiaomi-TabLDM further extends tabular prediction through test-time compute scaling, where allocating additional computation at inference time consistently improves predictive performance over the base model.

report.summary: Xiaomi-TabLDM is a new tabular foundation model achieving top regression performance via synthetic causal pretraining and in-context learning, without fine-tuning.
report.background: Tabular data—rows and columns—dominates everyday business and scientific applications, but foundation models have historically focused on text and images. Recently, models like TabPFN have shown that tabular tasks can be handled by in-context learning, avoiding costly task-specific fine-tuning. Xiaomi-TabLDM pushes this further by pretraining exclusively on synthetic data generated from structural causal models (SCMs). Rather than relying on real-world data, SCMs generate diverse, causally coherent tables that force the model to learn general feature interactions. To handle this data efficiently, the authors introduce three-stage training, dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual modules, and a sparse mixture-of-experts design. The result is a model that performs exceptionally well on regression benchmarks while using far less training and inference compute, and it even improves with test-time scaling.
key_points: SOTA performance with less compute. On the OpenML-CTR23 benchmark, Xiaomi-TabLDM ranks first for regression; across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO it places second. In TabArena, it reaches near-top Elo using 82% less training time and 68% less inference time than the leading TabFM, suggesting superior efficiency.

Synthetic-only pretraining. TabLDM is trained purely on synthetic tabular data generated from structural causal models. This approach creates a vast diversity of controlled data and avoids privacy and labeling issues. The authors argue this enables more flexible context use during in-context prediction, making the model robust to new tabular tasks without fine-tuning.

Architecture advances. The model combines three-stage training, dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts. Dual-stream grouping separates different feature types, while sparse MoE allows efficient specialization on diverse tasks. These components help capture rich interactions between columns and enable large-scale capacity scaling.

Test-time scaling helps. Xiaomi-TabLDM supports test-time compute scaling: giving the model more inference compute (e.g., more forward passes or internal reasoning) reliably boosts prediction accuracy over the base model. This mirrors LLM test-time scaling techniques and gives practitioners a knob to trade extra compute for better accuracy.
report.impact: Tabular data modeling remains essential in finance, healthcare, and retail, but most deep models require retraining per dataset. Xiaomi-TabLDM demonstrates that a single pretrained model, trained on synthetic causal data, can solve classification and regression tasks via in-context learning alone. This could reduce the time and expertise needed to build reliable prediction pipelines, and its better compute efficiency makes foundation models practical for mid-size companies, not just cloud scale. For developers, it enables fast prototyping and cheap inference. For regular users, applications like credit scoring, demand forecasting, or medical risk assessment could become more accurate on small datasets without custom model training. The test-time scaling option further empowers decision-makers to balance latency and accuracy.
report.tools: For readers wanting to follow up, keep an eye on Xiaomi's AI research GitHub for model weights. Meanwhile, the closest open-source baseline is TabPFN (prior-fitted network) on GitHub, offering tabular in-context learning. The paper cites benchmarks TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO, and OpenML for datasets. PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers are the likely deployment frameworks if the model is released under a permissive license.
